subject: Budget range validation - Lyra Finance (monthly token bands & procurement thresholds)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@lyra-finance.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo - follow-up (token volumes & budget)

Hey Liam - thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a couple of asks so we can get a formal quote over to procurement: 

What I heard from you:
- Primary use: real-time customer support summarization + routing + post-call insights.
- Usage profile: peak hours with bursts during end-of-month reconciliation windows.
- Initial target model class: a moderately-capable open model (we recommended Redwood-curated mid-tier variant).
- Expected volume: ballpark 20-30M tokens/month in month one, with potential to scale to 50M+ by Q3 depending on lift.

Open items we need to lock for quoting and SOW: 
1) Confirm a monthly spend band you are comfortable with (e.g., <$10k, $10k-$25k, $25k-$50k, $50k+). This helps us pick the right reserved capacity vs hosted mix and show unit economics.
2) Procurement threshold: what approval/PO level triggers formal procurement at Lyra (we discussed $25k vs $50k thresholds).
3) Any required contract terms (SLA, data residency, SOC2) - we can surface standard language and an SOW.

Quick note on unit economics to set expectations: our typical hosted unit economics for the mid-tier model are in the $300-$600 per 1M tokens range depending on batching and KV-cache hit rates. For reserved/dedicated capacity (committed) we can reduce that by ~30-50% at higher commits. I'll put a simple example in the next email.

Attachments: I attached a quick token estimate template (Lyra_token_estimates.xlsx) - please fill in any more accurate volume slices if you have them.

Next steps: can you confirm the monthly spend band and procurement threshold? If procurement needs an SOW/quote, loop in procurement and I'll send a one-page SOW + formal quote.

Thanks -
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@lyra-finance.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@lyra-finance.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Intro + demo - follow-up (token volumes & budget)

Thanks Marissa - nice to meet you on the call. Quick answers below: 

1) Monthly spend band: based on current projections, Lyra is planning an initial monthly run-rate in the $8k-$15k band (we're conservative for month 1 while we ramp). By Q3 we expect to be in the $30k-$45k band if metrics look good.
2) Procurement threshold: our procurement team requires a formal PO for any supplier spend over $25k. For <$25k we can onboard via standard vendor setup without a PO but still need a quote and T&Cs.
3) Contract terms: SOC 2 Type II is required, and we prefer US data residency for customer PII. We will likely want a 30-day SLA review clause but nothing extreme to start.

For volume: our initial estimate (filled in the template) shows ~25M tokens/month average (mix of prompts and responses). I attached the updated Lyra_token_estimates.xlsx with the breakdown.

Procurement (cc'd) - can you confirm what the standard Redwood onboarding package looks like (SOW + quote + W-9)? Also any lead times for a PO >$25k?

Liam
Head of Product
Lyra Finance
liam@lyra-finance.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@lyra-finance.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lyra-finance.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo - follow-up (token volumes & budget)

Thanks - this is super helpful, Liam. Per your numbers, FYI here's a clear worked example so procurement has something to evaluate alongside their thresholds. I'll keep it conservative (lower-bound batching & cache).

Example pricing scenarios (mid-tier model, hosted API):
- Scenario A - Conservative (no reserved commit, minimal KV cache hit): $550 / 1M tokens
  * 25M tokens/mo -> $13,750/mo
  * Annualized -> ~$165k
- Scenario B - Moderate (some caching, light batching): $420 / 1M tokens
  * 25M tokens/mo -> $10,500/mo
  * Annualized -> ~$126k
- Scenario C - Committed Reserved (6-12 month commit, dedicated pool) -> effective $260 / 1M tokens (includes 35% commit discount + improved batching)
  * 25M tokens/mo -> $6,500/mo
  * Annualized -> ~$78k

Notes and considerations:
- The big drivers: batching profile (latency SLO vs throughput), prefix/KV cache hit rates, and whether you want reserved capacity for predictable throughput.
- Given Lyra's $25k PO threshold, Scenario A or B would be handled via hosted invoice (no PO required if under $25k/mo), but once you cross $25k/mo we recommend moving to a reserved commit to get better unit economics and to make procurement simpler (committed contract + monthly invoice).
- If you want a target comparative metric, we usually talk to customers about target $/1M tokens they want to hit - for many mid-market fintechs that target is $200-$350 / 1M tokens after commit discounts. If Lyra is aiming for $30k-$45k/mo in Q3, you should be able to reach that range with a modest commit and optimized caching.

Attachments: I attached Redwood_pricing-options-v1.pdf and a draft one-page SOW (Lyra_SOW_v1.pdf). The SOW is intentionally light - scope, 3-month ramp plan, and acceptance criteria. If procurement wants changes, point to the SOW section numbers in the reply.

Next steps: 
- Liam/procurement: confirm whether you want a 6- or 12-month commit option priced in the quote (we can include both).
- If PO >$25k required: we'll prepare a formal quote + SOW + W-9 and send it to procurement.
- Internal: Dylan, can you prepare a quick committed pricing line for 6- and 12-month terms at 25M and 50M token bands? I can attach that to the quote.

Thanks -
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Great, this is exactly what procurement needs. Procurement - we are happy to evaluate both 6- and 12-month commit options; Marissa, please include a 25M and 50M token band pricing table and call out the effective $/1M token after the commit discount. Also please attach the W-9 and the standard SOC 2 attestation.

Procurement note on lead time: PO approvals typically take 7-10 business days once a formal quote and SOW are submitted. For PO >$25k we will route through legal for standard review, which may add another 5-7 business days.

Liam
